subject: RE: Freedom of Information / Historical Records Request - Mr. Williams, Cardiff Post Office Engineering Department, 1897 Marconi Lavernock Experiments
body_text:
Dear Retired Sergeant Buckler,

As my colleague Kate has advised, Royal Mail are not, and have not since 2013, been subject to the FOIA. We are not bound by that legislation as it only applies to Public Authorities and Royal Mail is a private company.

It is the case that access to personal data is typically considered under the Right of Access, part of GDPR, however this legislation relates to data of identifiable living individuals and which is retained by a Data Controller at the point a request is made. Royal Mail do not hold records relating to its employees (or that of its previous company names) from 1897 - as Kate explained it might be the case that some of this historic information is held by the Postal Museum (as part of the Archives) but they are a separate legal entity and we have no knowledge of or access to the records they choose to retain for historical purposes.

We would urge you to contact the postal museum directly - records relating to 1897 are unlikely to constitute personal data (as those to whom records relate are likely to be sadly no longer with us) and a matter of public record.

For the avoidance of doubt we, Royal Mail, would not hold records from 1897 relating to your Grandfather.

Kind Regards

Daniel Tulp
Privacy Manager
Information Governance and Group Data Protection Office

From: Sion Buckler <hywelapbuckler@gmail.com>
Sent: 02 September 2026 03:56
To: irgt <irgt@royalmail.com>
Subject: Re: Freedom of Information / Historical Records Request - Mr. Williams, Cardiff Post Office Engineering Department, 1897 Marconi Lavernock Experiments


Dear Ms Watkinson,

Thank you for your response.

I should clarify that my enquiry was made as a Freedom of Information request concerning recorded information relating to Mr Williams, the Cardiff Post Office Engineering Department, and the 1897 Marconi experiments at Lavernock. It was not simply a request for general historical guidance.

I appreciate that the Postal Museum may hold relevant historical material. However, if Royal Mail does not hold any of the requested information, I would be grateful if you could confirm that explicitly as the response to my FOI request.

If Royal Mail does hold relevant information, please process the request under the Freedom of Information Act 2000 and provide the information, subject to any applicable exemptions.

If Royal Mail considers that the Freedom of Information Act does not apply to this particular request, please explain the basis for that position and identify the relevant provision or status on which you rely.

I would therefore be grateful if you could reconsider the response as an FOI request and provide a substantive response confirming whether Royal Mail holds any relevant recorded information, rather than simply directing me to another archive.

Kind regards,



Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)

Royal Signals Cyber/ Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member

Subject: Re: Freedom of Information / Historical Records Request - Mr. Williams, Cardiff Post Office Engineering Department, 1897 Marconi Lavernock Experiments


Kate,

Thank you for clarifying Royal Mail Group's position regarding the Freedom of Information Act.

I understand that following privatisation in 2013, Royal Mail is no longer subject to statutory FOIA obligations. I am not seeking to dispute that point.

My enquiry is principally concerned with the historical GPO records themselves, dating from around 1897. I would therefore be grateful if you could confirm whether Royal Mail Group, its heritage/archive function, or any predecessor records system nevertheless retains, or has information concerning the custody or transfer of, pre-privatisation personnel or engineering records from the 1890s.

Specifically, I am seeking:

  *   Any personnel, service or establishment records for a Mr Williams employed in the Cardiff Post Office engineering/telegraph department circa 1897;
  *   Any internal correspondence, memoranda, engineering reports or other records relating to the department's involvement in Guglielmo Marconi's wireless telegraphy experiments at Lavernock Point in May 1897, including the erection of the approximately 120-foot pole/aerial installation;
  *   Any records originating from the former General Post Office (GPO) engineering or Telegraph Department which may have remained with, or subsequently been transferred from, Royal Mail Group.

If Royal Mail Group does not hold such records, I would be grateful if you could confirm whether there is any information available concerning their subsequent archival destination or transfer - for example, whether relevant GPO engineering/Telegraph Department records were transferred to The Postal Museum and Archive, The National Archives, BT Heritage/BT Archives, or another repository.

I will, as you suggest, contact The Postal Museum and Archive directly in parallel. However, because the individual concerned was associated with the GPO engineering/telegraph function rather than ordinary postal delivery, any guidance you can provide regarding the provenance and present location of those technical records would be particularly helpful.

I am also happy to provide further identifying information concerning Mr Williams, including approximate dates and his association with Great House Farm, Llandough, if that would assist in identifying the individual or records concerned.

Thank you again for your assistance. Even if Royal Mail no longer holds the records themselves, confirmation of their historical custody or transfer would be extremely useful in directing the research to the correct repository.

Kind regards,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)

Royal Signals Cyber and Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member
